# Introducing Cogent Security

Cogent exits stealth with $11M in funding and a thesis: the hardest part of vulnerability management is everything after the scan.

Jul 14, 2025, 4 min read, Vineet Edupuganti, Co-Founder and CEO

## The First AI Taskforce for Vulnerability Management

Cogent Security is redefining how enterprises stay ahead of today’s relentless wave of vulnerabilities and exploits. We’re slashing remediation times, eliminating manual effort, and delivering real business impact, already protecting millions of assets across the Fortune 500 and beyond.

Today, we’re thrilled to launch out of stealth with $11 million in funding and the backing of world-class investors and advisors across security, enterprise software, and AI.

## Vulnerability Management Is at a Breaking Point

For decades, identifying and fixing vulnerabilities has been a cornerstone of enterprise cybersecurity. But in today’s rapidly evolving threat landscape, that cornerstone is cracking:

- Nearly 45,000 CVEs were published this year alone, 4x more than a decade ago¹
- Vulnerability exploitation is now the fastest growing cause of breaches globally per Verizon DBIR²
- Threat actors are moving faster than ever, cutting time-to-exploit in half thanks to generative AI³

Today we're announcing Autonomous Vulnerability Response (AVR), the first end-to-end autonomous AI vulnerability response capability proven in production. Most vulnerability management tools stop at the ticket. AVR runs the whole loop as one continuous process: 1. Detection: agentless, catches zero day exposures within ~10 minutes of disclosure. 2. Investigation: gathers evidence across the environment, correlates against asset ownership and compensating controls, produces a findings package with reasoning preserved. 3. Remediation: generates the fix, scores change impact, dispatches through Jira or ServiceNow, and executes under customer guardrails. 4. Validation: independently confirms the fix through a scanner rescan or SBOM rebuild. If it didn't hold, the ticket reopens automatically. Where customer policy allows, the loop runs without human intervention. Where policy requires oversight, humans stay in. The video below is with Corey Kaemming(CISO, Valvoline Instant Oil Change) and Shawn Kerns(Head of InfoSec, University of the Pacific), two of the practitioners running AVR in production. Today we’re introducing Cogent Community, a free solution for security practitioners. Community brings our agentic AI together with VulnCheck, the premier source for open vulnerability and exploit intelligence, so defenders can level the playing field against AI-enabled adversaries. As we worked with customers to understand their pain points across the vulnerability management lifecycle, we uncovered a major bottleneck. Teams were losing hours each day on vulnerability research just to answer three questions: what’s going on in the wild, is this relevant to us, and what do we do next? By the time the picture was clear, other fires were already burning. So, we trained agents to become experts in curating, analyzing, and guiding action on vulnerability and exploit intelligence. Practitioners get precious time back, while the heavy lift of research and synthesis gets picked up by AI. # Startup Cogent Comes to Vulnerability Management Armed with AI Agents

July 23, 2025

Share

By Jeffrey Burt

(Adobe Stock)

The vulnerability management space is a fast-growing and crowded one, with the global market expected to grow to as much as$24.04 billion by 2030, driven by the need to protect enterprise data and remain compliant in an expanding regulatory environment. It is a space dominated by heavyweights like Qualys, Rapid7, Cisco Systems, and Tenable - all competing to helping enterprises stay ahead of the next vulnerability.

Despite this, Vineet Edupuganti and the other founders of Cogent Security saw an opportunity to elbow their way into the competitive sector, with expanding generative AI technologies, including agentic AI, as the way to do it.

“A core piece of what makes Cogent different is that we are AI-native, and also plug into the broader ecosystem,” Edupuganti, the company’s CEO, told MSSP Alert. “Many existing solutions operate within siloed walled gardens, whether due to strategic or technical reasons. Cogent is able to pull together telemetry from a range of sources – [such as] vulnerability scanners, CNAPP [cloud native application protection platforms], and EDR [endpoint detection and response] – and stitch this together.”

# One of my biggest takeaways from building Cogent is that AI is making intelligence cheaper, but context and trust are becoming more valuable. | Vineet Edupuganti · LinkedIn · 2026-08-20

**Vineet Edupuganti**: Co-Founder and CEO at Cogent Security with 1 year of total professional experience. Previous roles include Head of Multi Product Platform Division at Abnormal AI. Based in San Francisco, California, United States [US].

---

One of my biggest takeaways from building [Cogent](https://linkedin.com/company/cogentsecurity) is that AI is making intelligence cheaper, but context and trust are becoming more valuable.

The most interesting problems aren’t where off-the-shelf AI already works well. They’re where you need deep, proprietary enterprise context, the cost of being wrong is high, and the bar for taking action is even higher.

Cybersecurity, and vulnerability remediation in particular, is a great example. Being right 90% of the time isn’t good enough when you’re deciding what to fix or making changes to production systems. You need to deeply understand the environment, make high-confidence decisions, and earn the trust to act on them.

As models continue to commoditize, the hardest AI problems will be the most defensible: the ones where being wrong is expensive and earning the right to take action is hard.
